clue.text: Scientist came across a lot of magnetism with substance

parts.note: to come across someone is to meet them, past tense here

indicators.note: a lot of a word, not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: allure is attractive power, a kind of magnetism
the gist is the substance or essence of something

explanation.surface: A scientist encounters lots of magnetism in some material.
explanation.definitionFit: A metallurgist is a scientist who studies metals and their properties.

clue.text: Dress caught on a black taxi

parts.note: a mini is a short dress
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's dress gets snagged on a black cab.
explanation.walkthrough: A minicab is a British private-hire taxi that must be booked rather than hailed.
explanation.definitionFit: A minicab is a type of hired car, a taxi booked by phone.

clue.text: Running into maltreated ragamuffin

indicators.note: running here means set loose and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fourteen letters of these two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A scruffy urchin who has been badly treated runs into someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A tatterdemalion is a person in ragged clothes, a synonym for a scruffy urchin.

clue.text: Parasite left on tree, destroying billions

indicators.note: destroying the billions means that letter is wiped out of the tree

parts.note: the beech is a common tree

explanation.surface: A parasite is left clinging to a tree, wrecking billions of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A leech is a blood-sucking worm, the classic parasite.

clue.text: Put mares out towards spring. perhaps

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

parts.note: the eight letters of these two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Horses are turned out to pasture as spring approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season, but it is a water source: going upstream heads towards a river's source.
explanation.definitionFit: Upstream means moving against the current, towards the source of a river, which may be a spring.

clue.text: I invested in horse over win

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, like money put into a venture
in a down clue, over means the horse word is turned upside down

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
taken as written

explanation.surface: A punter puts money on a horse, hoping for a win.
explanation.definitionFit: To gain is to win or obtain something, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: State of fruit ends in great wastage

parts.note: a sultana is a dried grape

indicators.note: the ends in the two following words means their final letters

parts.note: the last letters of these two words are taken

explanation.surface: A grim report on how much fruit is thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultanate is a country or state ruled by a sultan.

clue.text: Plain short stage show's got excess of parts

indicators.note: short means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: overt means plain, open to view
a production is a staged theatrical show

explanation.surface: A simple short theatre show has too many roles for its cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts' suggests acting roles, but in the definition it means manufactured components.
explanation.definitionFit: Overproduction is making more items or components than are needed.

clue.text: Idly read lines in bed, mostly

indicators.note: in places the lines inside the shortened bed
mostly means most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: taken as written, then cut short
rows are lines of things

explanation.surface: Someone lazily reads a few lines while lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To browse is to look through a book casually, reading without concentration.

clue.text: Explosive ingredient some disconcertingly brought round

indicators.note: brought round means turned back to front
some of the word, a run of its letters, is taken

parts.note: the run of letters sits in the middle of this word

explanation.surface: A worrying discovery of some explosive material being transported.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre, potassium nitrate, is saltpetre, a key component of gunpowder.

clue.text: Lighter finished as fluid escaped

definitions.note: a noun phrase: fluid that has escaped

parts.note: a spill is a thin strip of wood or paper used to light a fire
over means finished, at an end

explanation.surface: A cigarette lighter ran out because its fuel leaked away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' looks like the gadget, but here it is an old-fashioned spill for lighting candles or pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: A spillover is liquid or anything else that overflows its container.

clue.text: Cherish processed English cheese

indicators.note: processed, as with processed cheese, means the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: the seven letters of this word are the fodder

explanation.surface: A cheese lover cherishes a processed English cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheshire is a crumbly English cheese named after the county.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheshire is a traditional crumbly English cheese, an example of the category.

clue.text: Pub noise? This can carry

parts.note: a bar is a pub or drinking place
a row is a loud noise or din

explanation.surface: A rowdy pub, where something can carry the sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry' suggests noise carrying; the definition is a wheelbarrow, which carries loads.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrow is a small cart for transporting loads, so it is a thing that carries.

clue.text: Plots with skill turned over for plant used for stuffing

parts.note: garden beds are plots of ground

indicators.note: turned over means the following pair is read backwards

parts.note: art is skill or craft

explanation.surface: A gardener skilfully digs over plots for a plant used in upholstery.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedstraw is a herb once dried and used to fill mattresses, hence its name.

clue.text: Time to manage revolutionary concerning weapon

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
Che Guevara is the crossword's favourite revolutionary
on means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A revolutionary's time has come to deal with a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: A truncheon is a police officer's baton.
explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is a short club carried by police, a blunt weapon.

clue.text: Fantastic country is fine, with a lake

parts.note: taken as written
Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A tourist's verdict: a wonderful country with a nice lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' looks like praise; here it means of fantasy, a fairyland.
explanation.definitionFit: Faerie is the realm of the fairies, an imaginary land of fantasy.

clue.text: Standard form of gene mostly for twin

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: an allele is one of the variant forms of a gene

explanation.surface: Twins share a standard version of a gene for the most part.
explanation.definitionFit: Parallel as a noun means a counterpart or match, something that twins another.

clue.text: Note Mickey almost is universally recognised

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: almost signals the word stops just short of its last letter

parts.note: Mickey Mouse, Disney's cartoon character

explanation.surface: Mickey Mouse is pretty much known by everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous means widely known, recognised by almost everyone.

clue.text: Go without food, finding a trace of mercury in salmon?

indicators.note: in places the small additions inside the salmon

parts.note: a salmon is an example of a fish, hence the question mark
taken as written

indicators.note: a trace is just a tiny bit, here the first letter

parts.note: the word whose opening letter is the trace

explanation.surface: Someone goes hungry after finding mercury contamination in their salmon.
explanation.definitionFit: To famish is to starve, to suffer extreme hunger from lack of food.

clue.text: Perfume the French sell old queen

parts.note: la is a French word for the
to vend is to sell
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: A French perfume seller deals with an elderly queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavender is a fragrant plant and the scent made from it, used as a perfume.

clue.text: Ice to keep fresh without power

indicators.note: without means the power letter is left out

parts.note: to preserve food is to keep it fresh

explanation.surface: Ice is used to keep things fresh when the electricity is off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ice' looks like frozen water; here it is coldness of manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve is a cool, aloof manner, like the iciness of a reticent person.

clue.text: Desire to do mischief in country church

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A wish to cause trouble in a rural church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country church' reads as a village church, but the words split into a nation and an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the intention to harm others, ill will.

clue.text: Obstruct idiot grabbing copper in war-torn city

parts.note: to dam is to block or obstruct a flow

indicators.note: grabbing means the idiot holds the copper inside

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot snatches copper and gets in the way in a war zone.
explanation.walkthrough: CU is the chemical symbol for copper.
explanation.definitionFit: Damascus is the Syrian capital, a city scarred by the civil war.

clue.text: Very much into morning working, then golf

definitions.note: a preposition phrase meaning in the midst of

parts.note: on means operating, working

explanation.surface: Someone keen on morning work followed by a round of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very much into' looks like keen on; it means deep in the middle of.
explanation.definitionFit: Among means surrounded by or in the thick of a group.

clue.text: Bamboo vessel, not round

indicators.note: not means the round letter is excluded

parts.note: a canoe is a small boat

explanation.surface: A bamboo boat that isn't circular.
explanation.definitionFit: Bamboo stems are canes, hollow jointed stalks of grass.

clue.text: Bat defensively, a single wicket in stand

indicators.note: in means placed inside the stand

parts.note: a stall is a stand at a market
one is a single unit

explanation.surface: A batsman playing safe at the crease while a single wicket falls.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, to stonewall is to bat purely to avoid getting out, not to score.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonewalling is blocking each ball patiently, the cautious defensive batting style.

clue.text: Tree, large, that is beside river

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size
ie is the Latin abbreviation id est, that is

explanation.surface: A big tree stands beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The osier is a willow, a riverside tree whose shoots are used in basketry.

clue.text: Excitedly telling niece news

indicators.note: excitedly suggests the letters are agitated into a new order

parts.note: the twelve letters of these two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly tells their niece the latest news.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence means information, as in military intelligence gathered about events.
